name: markdown-sections-as-symbols
body:
Markdown headings must map to graph symbols. Each heading becomes a Struct section symbol; containment is the section hierarchy under the file: the File contains every top-level heading Struct (File→Struct is a legal pair), and every deeper heading is contained by the nearest preceding lower-level heading, else by the File (Struct→Struct). The schema nests symbols only through Struct, so a section is a Struct. There is NO synthesized document-root Struct: it existed solely to anchor whole-document/preamble links, and links are DEFERRED (requirements.note.markdown-links-deferred), so a heading-less document yields no section Struct — only its File node.

The FQN scheme must be injective by construction: a genuine same-kind Struct/Function collision fails loudly (`claim` panics, src/ingest.rs:88-96) rather than overwriting, while a Module-level collision is SILENTLY shadowed and dropped (src/ingest.rs:647-670) — silent data loss, not a loud failure, so an injective scheme is the only safe guard. The scheme is anchored on the file's absolute path, never on a dot-joined directory/file-stem prefix: a markdown Module's FQN is `<language-root>.` + the directory's absolute path (i.e. `md.<absolute-path>` under language rooting); a markdown File's FQN is the file's absolute path, so the extension is retained and `docs/README.md` and `docs/README.markdown` are distinct; a heading section's FQN extends its parent section's FQN as `<parent-section-fqn>.<section>` where `<section>` is the heading's slug, and a top-level heading section's parent is the File FQN (so its FQN is `<file-fqn>.<section>`). Dot-joining a directory path is explicitly rejected as the lossy alternative that aliases `docs/guide` and `docs.guide` to the same `docs.guide` prefix.

The slug rule is DECIDED (GitHub-style; requirements.constraint.markdown-slug-rule): it maps heading text to exactly ONE FQN segment that never embeds the `.` separator (`.` is dropped), and maps duplicate headings in one file to distinct segments by construction. Uniqueness is assigned in document order against the set of segments already assigned: each heading's segment is the first free candidate in a sequence generated from its own RAW bare slug (the raw-slug candidate space, not the cooked slugs), so `# Overview`, `# Overview`, `# Overview 1` render `overview`, `overview-1`, `overview-2` — the third heading's raw `overview-1` is taken, so its trailing number is incremented, not a second counter appended to the cooked slug. The rule is total: an empty normalization falls back to the pinned literal `section`, which participates in dedup like any other bare slug (`section`, `section-1`, …). Because every segment is drawn from the complement of the already-assigned set and is a single delimiter-free segment, the mapping is injective within a document — no two sections in a document render the same FQN segment — and, with the unique absolute-path File prefix (absolute paths are unique per file and per directory), no two documents or directories render the same section FQN. AC: a document with nested headings yields one Struct per heading, each contained by the File or the nearest preceding lower-level heading; a document with no headings yields no section Struct (only its File node); the same-stem fixture (`docs/README.md` and `docs/README.markdown`, each with a `## Overview`) and the path-alias fixture (`docs/guide/x.md` and `docs.guide/x.md`) yield distinct section FQNs; the duplicate-heading fixtures yield distinct section Structs — two identical `## Overview` headings render `overview` and `overview-1`, and `## Overview`, `## Overview`, `## Overview 1` render `overview`, `overview-1`, `overview-2` — so no two sections in a document share an FQN segment and the same-kind Struct collision that panics `claim` (src/ingest.rs:88-96) cannot arise; the scan reports zero shadowed modules (no module prefix silently shadowed or merged, src/ingest.rs:647-670) and the fixtures produce no residual same-kind section collision (which would panic in `claim`, src/ingest.rs:88-96).
